pk.context: 0.5 mg intravenous, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A 1.5-to-2-day half-life and a 475 to 500 L volume of distribution set this cardiac glycoside apart.

clues.text: About 25% is bound to plasma protein. Only 13% of a dose is metabolized, and 50 to 70% of an intravenous dose is excreted unchanged in the urine.
Molecular weight 780.95. It is practically insoluble in water and in ether, and its crystals melt with decomposition above 230 °C.
Approved under an NDA as injections of 250 mcg/mL for adults and 100 mcg/mL for children, in single-dose ampules or vials.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in ventricular fibrillation and in known hypersensitivity to it or related preparations; adverse reactions are reported in 5 to 20%.
Mild to moderate heart failure in adults, contractility in pediatric heart failure, and resting ventricular rate control in chronic atrial fibrillation.
Inhibits the Na-K ATPase sodium pump, raising intracellular calcium in the myocardium, which increases inotropy and slows conduction.
The generic name begins with D and has seven letters.
